bet.text: Shoot while moving, at any angle: a turret with at least one full rotation on a robot that decides by itself when to shoot.

demand.text: The team planned from day one on shooting while moving, because the game is called Rapid React and there is a lot of defense. It wanted a climber that reaches the traversal rung with the fewest actions.

auto.text: Analysts describe a five-ball auto in an ISR 1 quarterfinal and in the Carver division finals.

cycle.text: The single driver collects cargo. Belts stow the first ball under the shooter and hold the second at the handoff. The robot decides when to shoot, also while moving, unless the driver presses a button that stops it. It shoots opponent cargo away from the goal automatically.

endgame.text: From the mid rung straight to the traversal rung: the telescope pulls the robot up, an arm that goes against the truss lifts it at an angle that lets a hook take the traversal rung, then the telescope lets go.

fallback.text: The driver can stop the automatic shot, and the position estimate can be readjusted manually.
In one ISR 1 quarterfinal the robot kept shooting instead of climbing; an analyst counted nine endgame shots and six scored, three points short of a traversal climb.

gave_up.text: Moving the center of mass slowly between rungs costs 2 to 3 seconds, and in February the climber could not let go of the mid rung early. The robot must be placed very precisely left to right on the bar.
A commenter calls its shoot-on-the-fly and turret game changing, but says 254, 1678 and 1323 missed noticeably fewer shots, and a miss took scarce cargo out of play.

changed.text: After balls jumped out of the hub at the first event, the team built a new shooter with a top roller in one week. Aiming took the most time in the climb there, so it added a camera arm. Skid detection came before the championship.
Observers say the turret fell off in a championship practice match, during auto rather than on impact, and was back before the first match.

outcome.text: 63-7-0 in official play; finalist in the Carver division; ranked 10 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 59.22, Carver).

solves.text: Run bevel gears near the carpet without grease, which would pick up dirt

facts.text: The same module as the season before, with a self-made aluminum wheel
The smaller bevel gear is brass and the larger is aluminum anodized with a Teflon-infused ceramic coating

functions.name: Clutch intake
functions.type: rigid deployed intake with a compliant drive

solves.text: Take impacts without breaking the robot or the intake motor, and without frequent replacement

facts.text: A lever on the driven sprocket pulls the arm through surgical tubing, so the arm collapses back into the robot on impact
The robot uses no pneumatics
The intake shares a Falcon with the floor belts

solves.text: Know where each ball is and what color it is, so the robot can shoot or eject it

facts.text: The floor belts share the intake's Falcon and the vertical belts have their own, so the feed to the shooter is controlled
Three IR sensors mark the entrance, the handoff between belts and the stow position just under the shooter
The entrance sensor also lets the robot detect and eject a third ball
After the first ball is stowed the intake runs until a second reaches the handoff, then stops
The color is read only after the IR sensor sees the ball, at a distance of about
The ball advances only when thresholds on magnitude and red to blue ratio are met
IR sensor: an LED and a phototransistor, with a 100 ohm resistor on the LED and a 10k ohm pullup
Color sensor: REV

functions.name: Turret
functions.type: turret with more than one rotation

solves.text: Shoot at any angle at any time

facts.text: The gearbox is at the bottom of the robot and drives the turret through a pipe, for a low center of mass
Driven by two Falcons
Target travel was about 420 to 450 degrees; the practice robot had about 380 to 400, and the competition robot a longer wire and sleeve for more
It runs on six shoulder bolts with three bearings each, the base plate sandwiched between the larger top and bottom bearings
The cable runs in a durable sleeve with both ends directed by 3D printed parts
It wraps around near its limits; the margin depends on whether the robot holds balls or is ready to shoot

cost.text: Overshoots, rare, on fast motions such as wrap-around, from the turret's inertia and the spinning wheel's angular momentum
In February the team was not entirely comfortable with the cable arrangement, though it had not pinched or caught

functions.name: Shooter and hood
functions.type: single flywheel with adjustable hood and top roller

solves.text: Keep balls from jumping out of the hub

facts.text: The top roller came with the shooter built after the first event
Before that rebuild: wheel of three 6 in WCP aluminum wheels with the black roughtop tread of the drive wheels
Before that rebuild: the hood backing was uncoated SLS nylon 12
Before that rebuild: compression went from 1.5 in to 1 in along the hood, only because that was easier to build
At the reveal: shots up to about 4 m tended not to bounce out; from either alliance wall every 2 to 3 balls did

solves.text: Find hood angle and wheel speed for every distance and robot velocity, with a shooter whose ball spin changes with its speed

facts.text: Models gravity, air drag and the Magnus force, with equations from a paper on shooting tennis balls
For each distance and robot velocity it picks the trajectory least sensitive to small errors, with a preference for lower ones that bounce out less
It runs off the robot; polynomials up to third degree give hood pitch and wheel speed from distance and radial velocity
The tangential velocity is subtracted from the 3D shot vector
One commenter counted 36 teleop cargo in a championship match, another 34

functions.name: Truss reactor climber
functions.type: telescope plus arm braced on the truss

solves.text: Reach the traversal rung with the fewest actions

facts.text: Two main actions: the telescope pulls the robot up while the V-shaped truss reactor goes against the truss and a hook takes the traversal rung; then the telescope lets go
The center of mass moves slowly from under the mid rung to under the traversal rung
Tested early with an improvised truss on the team version of the field

cost.text: The robot must be very precisely placed left to right; in February the mid rung could not be released early

solves.text: Aiming at the bar took the most time of the climb

facts.text: A small arm on a carbon tube is released when the truss reactor falls, and a rubber band opens it
Its camera looks at a line on the floor, so the robot gets parallel to it and at a set distance

solves.text: Know the robot's position when a wall or defender makes the wheels unreliable

facts.text: Merges the encoders (about 12 in the captions), the gyro and the Limelight
A wheel moving much faster than the robot's calculated motion is probably skidding, and odometry uses the other wheels
After a skid, odometry gets less weight and shooting is blocked until the camera has seen the target and agrees with the estimate

cost.text: A recap video says the positioning system had some issues in one Carver qualification match

solves.text: Tell the driver the robot's state and its sensor and subsystem faults

facts.text: Hall sensors on turret and hood are compared with the encoders; a mismatch declares a fault
The hood resets on the hall sensor or on motor current above a threshold
Blink speed shows the number of balls, green an opponent ball being shot, red a fault
A photo posted in September 2022 shows guards on the intake side just tall enough to protect the swerve modules, and taller ones at the other corners

decisions.choice: Shooting while moving, planned from day one
decisions.because: the game would have a lot of defense

decisions.choice: A rigid intake with a clutch
decisions.because: the flexible one had to be replaced many times
decisions.instead_of: the flexible intake of the season before

decisions.because: testing every distance at every velocity seemed impossible
decisions.instead_of: a map of measured shots by distance

decisions.because: the turret's inertia, the spinning wheel and unpredictable motion while driving need high acceleration
it has only two main actions to reach the traversal rung
decisions.cost: the robot must be very precisely placed left to right on the bar

decisions.choice: Moving the center of mass gradually between rungs
decisions.because: the team was not sure the robot or the driver station wall would survive a fast swing
the team saw no other way to shoot on the run and under defense
decisions.instead_of: no turret, as the year before, good enough for static shooting spots and safe zones
